labels.label: [4.CT] the cosmological time (prose, Bonsante's results quoted without proof)

hypotheses.paper: Λ has at least 2 elements (Def 4.4, l.900-901: 'If Λ contains at least 2 elements, then Ω±(Λ), if nonempty, is regular'; standing convention l.1001-1004: closed Λ 'not reduced to one point')
hypotheses.note: two elements with DISTINCT null directions (CosmoRegular.two). The paper's condition is too weak: two elements may share a direction, and the printed boundedness then fails (not_cosmoBoundedAsPrinted, Λ = {(u,0),(u,1)}). CosmoRegular.two is Bonsante's Def 4.1 (two non-parallel null support planes)

hypotheses.paper: sup over future timelike curves from ∂Ω
hypotheses.note: read on straight segments (the reverse triangle inequality makes them maximal); the curve form is not stated, the library's causal curves carry no proper time
continuousOn_cosmoTime plus strict monotonicity along ≤_⊤ and ≤_Ω; the library's IsTimeFunction (Causal/Morphism.lean:832) is global, with no On-version for an open set

findings: l.1049-1052 with Def 4.4 (l.900-901) and l.1001-1004: 'The proper times of all these curves are uniformly bounded' is false under the paper's own hypotheses on Λ (closed, at least 2 elements / not reduced to one point, future regular), for d >= 1 (Barbot's n >= 2): Λ = {(u,0),(u,1)} is closed, has two elements, is future regular with Ω⁺(Λ) = P⁺(u,0) (the second plane is parallel and redundant), and the proper times from the boundary to (1,0) are sqrt(2a-1), unbounded (not_cosmoBoundedAsPrinted, CosmoBoundedAsPrinted stated with IsClosed Λ, Λ.Nontrivial, FutureRegular Λ). The paper's 'at least 2 elements' does not imply Bonsante's two non-parallel null support planes (Bonsante Def 4.1), since two elements may share their null direction; so Barbot's 'completely equivalent' (l.921-922) is false and the condition should read 'Λ contains two elements with distinct null directions'. With that (CosmoRegular) the bound, the maximum and everything downstream hold.
l.1055: 'T(p) is equal to −sqrt(|p−π(p)|²)' should read sqrt(−|p−π(p)|²) (the printed form is minus the root of a negative number).
l.1064: the denominator of n(p) reads ⟨p−π(p) | p−n(p)⟩; it should be ⟨p−π(p) | p−π(p)⟩.
l.1058-1060: 'T is a C¹-convex function': T is concave as a function (its superlevel sets {T ≥ t} are convex); concavity is proved here (concaveOn_cosmoTime), C¹ is not.

Bonsante's results quoted at l.1053-1070 and l.1144-1145 that are PROVED here causally (DEC-36: no longer externals): uniqueness of π(p) (Prop 4.3), continuity of T, the level sets being spacelike (point-local c<1) entire Lipschitz graphs, the normal flow S(p+εn(p)) = S(p)+ε and S_{t+ε} = S_t + εn (Cor 4.5), T → 0 at ∂Ω, T → ∞ along every future-inextensible causal curve of Ω and T → 0 along every past-inextensible one, and Lemma 4.9 (every S_t is a Cauchy surface of Ω).
questions: Should Barbot's Def 4.4/4.5 (future regular, 'at least 2 elements') be amended to Bonsante's (two elements of Λ with distinct null directions), or should [4.CT] carry the hypothesis? The formalization carries it (CosmoRegular).
labels.note: T → ∞ along future-inextensible curves is proved in the one-sided (DEC-13) form exists_lt_cosmoTime_of_futureInextensible: for every B, T > B on a final segment of every FutureInextensible causal curve of Ω; the ray form tendsto_cosmoTime_add_smul is kept. isSpacelikeLipschitz_cosmoLevel is listed here only (it serves 4.14 as well).

labels.label: bprop:lip

hypotheses.paper: the hyperbolic metric on ℍⁿ⁻¹ and the induced Riemannian metric on S_t
hypotheses.note: chordal form: t²|n(p)−n(p')|² ≤ |p−p'|² for all p,p' ∈ S_t, with the Minkowski-form chord on both sides; the passage to the length metrics (inf of chord sums, l.1087-1091) is not proved

findings: Barbot's proof (ε < t, q(p) = p − εn(p), 'the convexity of S_{t−ε} implies the positivity', then ε → t) works directly at ε = t with q = π(p) ∈ ∂Ω: the positivity of ⟨π(p)−π(p') | n(p)−n(p')⟩ is the support property of π (minkB_cosmoRetract_le), and the dropped term |π(p)−π(p')|² ≥ 0 is the achronality of ∂Ω (minkQ_sub_nonneg_of_mem_frontier), which the proof uses silently.

labels.label: bprop:regular_cauchy_complete

hypotheses.note: NOT assumed: proved (bonsante_exhaustion, no sorry). The DEC-36 Prop Bonsante_exhaustion is kept as the curve content of Lemma 4.9 and is now a theorem for every CosmoRegular Λ, with the cone witness bonsante_exhaustion_cone (kb/0012). The 'here' value 'carried' records that the paper's citation is honoured, not that a hypothesis is added.

findings: Bonsante's Lemma 4.9, which Barbot cites without proof (l.1144-1145), has a short causal proof in the flat setting: an inextensible causal curve of Ω along which T ≤ B has bounded time coordinate (T(x)² ≥ 2(z₀ − ‖z⃗‖)(x − p)₀ on J⁺(p), z = p − r(p)), so it is Cauchy at its future end and converges to a point of J⁺(Ω) ⊆ Ω, where it extends; one along which T ≥ ε has time bounded below by the two null planes, converges at its past end to a point of cl Ω not on ∂Ω (T → 0 there), and extends. Only the W-local form of the library's extension lemma was missing; it is proved here (pastExtensible_of_tendsto_opens, futureExtensible_of_tendsto_opens).
labels.note: Globally hyperbolic: proved (FutureRegular.globallyHyperbolicOn, Penrose). Level sets Cauchy surfaces of Ω (IsCauchySurfaceOn), acausal, closed: proved, no sorry. Spacelike with point-local c<1: isSpacelikeLipschitz_cosmoLevel (listed under [4.CT]). Cauchy-complete: not stated (InducedLength not importable). The status stays partial for the completeness half and the CosmoRegular strengthening.

labels.label: bprop:agissons

hypotheses.note: any subgroup (any isometry) preserving Ω; discreteness and torsion-freeness are not used because only the invariance is proved

labels.note: Proved: T Γ-invariant, every S_t Γ-invariant, r equivariant. Not attempted: the isometric action on (S_t, induced length) (InducedLength not importable), proper discontinuity, freeness, the quotient Γ\Ω (another package).

kb_proposals: Lorentzian convexity does the analysis: the cosmological time is an inf of affine functions / concave, so ConcaveOn.continuousOn (Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Continuous) gives continuity and local Lipschitz for free; the support property of the maximiser replaces every derivative in Bonsante.

The bilinear lemmas minkB_add/sub/smul_left/right and minkQ_add/sub exist privately in Penrose, publicly in Isometries (in progress) and privately again in Cosmological: one public copy in Form at graduation.
A scaffold module whose .olean is missing (InducedLength at wave 4) is not importable by `lake env lean`; dispatches listing a module as 'built, importable' should check .lake/build/lib/lean first.

The library's extension-at-a-limit lemmas (pastExtensible_of_tendsto, extensible_of_tendsto) are for W = ⊤ only, but the W-local form is cheap: adjoin the limit in ⊤ (causalCurveIn_insert), restrict to W (CurveOn.restrict, image in W), prepend in W (exists_prepend works for any W). See Causal.Causality.pastExtensible_of_tendsto_opens / futureExtensible_of_tendsto_opens in Flat/Cosmological; they belong in Causal/Inextensible.lean at graduation.

To reach a finite open end, reparametrise by arctan (CausalCurveIn.arctanReparam): one argument then covers bounded and unbounded parameter intervals; FutureExtensible.of_comp is the missing twin of PastExtensible.of_comp.
